title: SWE-1.7: HARNESS-NATIVE
lede: July 8, 2026. The crossover point: a model trained directly inside the Devin agent harness, on tasks long enough that a single rollout blows past the context window. SWE-1.7 was the lab's first claim to frontier-level intelligence — at a fraction of frontier-level cost.
body:
## TRAINED WHERE IT WORKS Every SWE model before this one was trained for a harness. SWE-1.7 was trained inside one. The Devin agent loop — plan, act, observe, retry — became the RL environment itself, which is a different claim than ‘evaluated in Devin’: the gradient went through the real thing. ## THE TWO PROBLEMS LONG-HORIZON RL BRINGS * Context exhaustion — Devin tasks run long enough that rollouts exceed the raw context window; training had to teach the model to work beyond what it can literally see. * Reasoning bloat — RL on reasoning tasks tends to inflate response lengths (the DeepSeek R1 effect). SWE-1.7 was trained to elaborate only when the task is hard, keeping routine work cheap. ## THE NUMBERS ON THE PLACARD

## THE HISTORICAL FOOTNOTE SWE-1.7’s most durable contribution to the archive may be as a baseline. Two months later, the SWE-2 announcement measured itself against this model: 58% fewer turns, 81% lower cost, first code edit at step 18 instead of step 48. Every artifact in a museum eventually becomes the ruler a newer artifact is measured with. > From the start, we built Devin for completing asynchronous, long-running tasks. SWE-1.7 is trained directly in the Devin harness. — Cognition, July 2026 Final hall: SWE-2 — the model this lineage was rehearsing for.
